record.original_question: Is the class of linear lattices self-dual?

evidence.quote: [Haim1985, sec. 1.0] Is the class of linear lattices self-dual?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A lattice L is called a linear lattice (or lattice of commuting equivalence relations) if it is isomorphic to a sublattice of the lattice Eq(X) of equivalence relations on some set X, in which the join is given by relational composition; equivalently, L embeds into Eq(X) so that every pair of its elements, viewed as equivalence relations, commute under composition (R∘S = S∘R, in which case R∘S equals their join in Eq(X)).

For a lattice L = (L, ∧, ∨), its order dual L^op = (L, ∨, ∧) is the lattice obtained by interchanging meet and join. A class K of lattices is said to be self-dual if, for every L ∈ K, the dual lattice L^op also belongs to K (up to isomorphism).

Question: Is the class of all linear lattices self-dual? That is, whenever a lattice L is representable as a lattice of commuting equivalence relations on some set, is its order dual L^op also representable as a lattice of commuting equivalence relations on some (possibly different) set?
artifact.category_tag: Linear lattices and lattices of commuting equivalence relations
artifact.status_search_result: A recent survey on lattice properties (modular, Arguesian, linear, distributive) explicitly lists the self-duality of the class of linear lattices as an open question, alongside whether the class is a variety, whether it generates the variety of Arguesian lattices, and whether the free word problem is solvable. While Jónsson established that Arguesian lattices are self-dual, the corresponding question for linear lattices remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A survey of lattice properties: modular, Arguesian, linear, and distributive
status_evidence.snippet: While it remains an open question whether the class of all linear lattices is self-dual, there is an intrinsic duality to the list of deductions
status_evidence.claim: The self-duality of the class of linear lattices is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Linear lattice proof theory: An overview
status_evidence.snippet: Haiman developed a proof theory for implications valid in linear lattices, using graph-theoretic arguments to establish a duality theorem for this proof theory.
status_evidence.claim: There is a proof-theoretic duality but the structural self-duality of the class itself is not established.
